newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps-gasoline steals show with $4-5 rise.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps-gasoline steals show with $4-5 rise.

text.p: Gasoline shone as a beacon in the European oil swaps world on Wednesday.
Dealers said gasoline swaps were $4-5 a tonne stronger as surging NYMEX prices backed by stock data carried European prices higher. Tight supplies in European contributed to the bullish push.
Brent CFDs were essentially unchanged, but naphtha piggy-backed $1 higher on gasoline's strength. Fuel was also a touch stronger, but the star of the market was most certainly gasoline.
Dealers said August paper had a busy day with $203, $204, $205 and $204.50 all heard done with September trading at $193.50, $194 and $195.50.
"There is the U.S. strength plus the tightness in both NWE and Med so there's no reason for any immediate weakness," said one dealer.
Fresh wet supplies from August 15 onwards could dull gasoline's sparkle which was given an extra shine with a Turkish buy tender for 25,000 tonnes.
"I only see two cargoes available in August in the Mediterranean, that's tight," said one physical trader.
Other instruments had to take a back seat to gasoline.
Naphtha ticked up $1 or so on the back of gasoline's strength with August talked around $191.50 with September backwardated by $3-4 a tonne.
Heavy fuel edged tentatively higher with August valued around $91 with September 50-75 cents in contango.
Brent CFDs were almost unchanged with the balance of this week at +12 cents against September, August 4-8 at +3 cents, August 11-15 at - 4 cents and August 18-22 at -10 cents.
An August CFD traded at October Brent -7 cents and August 4-8 was done at September +4 cents.
Two rolls were also heard concluded. August 11-15 against 18-22 at +5 cents for a half cargo and August 6-12 against 19-25 at +12 cents.
